Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity call — initial notes

Thanks for the call today — good overview. A few quick clarifications from our side so you can size and price: 

- Target traffic: steady-state ~1.5B tokens / month, with peak months up to ~3B tokens.
- Typical request profile: average prompt+response ~700 tokens, median ~420 tokens.
- Concurrency/throughput: want ~150-200 requests/sec at peak, p99 latency target <300ms.
- Batch tolerance: we can tolerate batching up to ~150ms if it helps unit cost.
- Preferred GPU: we prefer H100 for quality/latency but will consider A100 if cost delta is large.
- Budget: preliminary internal range $50k–$120k / month depending on SLA and term.

Can you confirm rough $/1M token target you'd expect for a 12-month reserved commit at those volumes and a recommended GPU mix? Also please include any slot sizing guidance (number of GPUs) and whether you think a canary (2-week) pilot on Dedicated is feasible.

Thanks,
Alex
Head of AI Products | FinLytics

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity call — post-call recap & next steps

Alex — thanks for the clear numbers, that helps a lot. Recap of what we discussed + our follow-ups: 

Summary of your inputs (please confirm):
- Expected steady state: ~1.5B tokens / month; peak ~3B / month
- Request size: avg ~700 tokens; p99 latency target <300ms
- Concurrency: ~150-200 req/s at peak
- Preferred GPU: H100 preferred, open to A100 for cost optimization
- Budget band: $50k–$120k/month

Preliminary sizing (high level):
- For the profile above we recommend starting with a 4x H100 reserved pool as the baseline. That configuration gives headroom for your peak QPS and keeps KV cache locality good for chat-style workloads. If you want a cost-first option, 6x A100 (80GB) can often deliver comparable throughput for less cost but with slightly higher latency on some generation workloads.

Estimated unit economics (very rough, for 12-month reserved commit):
- 4x H100 reserved (monthly committed): target blended unit cost ~ $9–$14 per 1M tokens at steady state (volume-dependent).
- 6x A100 reserved (monthly committed): target blended unit cost ~ $7–$11 per 1M tokens.
- With annual billing and a 12+ month commit, we can push toward the lower end of those ranges.

Notes / assumptions:
- Estimates assume average request length ~700 tokens and utilization ~60–75% once steady.
- We assume conservative KV cache hit improvements (20% effective token reduction) for chat reuse; we can refine with a prompt sample set.
- Prices above exclude storage and premium SLAs (higher SLOs and retention add to cost).

Next steps I propose:
1) We’ll run a short Sizing/Throughput validation with your sample prompts to confirm the cache/hit and latency profile (Marcus and Dylan to scope).
2) We’ll provide an updated attachment with two priced options (4x H100 baseline, 6x A100 cost-optimized) and a 30-day canary plan.
3) If that looks good, we’ll put together a commercial term sheet + SOC2 & procurement packet.

I’ve attached an initial estimate (FinLytics_Dedicated_Estimate_v1.xlsx) and a PDF with baseline assumptions (redwood-dedicated-pricing-v2.pdf). Marcus and Dylan — can you please take point on the sizing runbook?

Thanks,

Alex — Marcus here (Platform & Performance). Quick note on the sizing + throughput validation we talked about:

Plan (what we'll run):
- Step 1: Collect representative prompt set (you can drop in the Drive link or send as a ZIP). Expected size ~200-300 samples covering short/medium/long.
- Step 2: Run load tests against a small dedicated staging pool: 1x H100 + 2x A100 staging split to measure latency and batching behavior.
- Step 3: Measure: tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU utilization, and effective KV cache hit rate.
- Step 4: Produce a throughput map showing GPUs -> supported QPS and token throughput for your profile.

Estimated time: ~5 business days once we have prompts & a test window. Can run the pilot in your VPC or in our dedicated staging — whichever you prefer.

Quick answer on canary: yes — a 14-30 day canary on a 2x H100 reserved (or equivalent) is feasible. Procurement typically wants SOC2 materials and an initial SOW; I’ll attach the SOC2 snapshot for procurement.

I’m looping Dylan for cost modeling (Dylan: can you generate the two price curves Marissa mentioned and include a 12-month vs 36-month commit comparison?).

Thanks — will follow up with the runbook and a link to the test plan tomorrow.
